description: FORK POSTURE. This repo is a long-lived fork of hyperdxio/hyperdx, so the
house default is inverted: dependency management covers ONLY the files WE
added. We do not own upstream's dependency tree, and bumping a transitive
dep in packages/*/package.json diverges us from upstream for a fix we did
not write, turns a pristine file into permanent rerere conflict surface
(docs/fork/design.md), and gets reverted or re-conflicted on the next sync.
SCOPED BY includePaths, NOT BY A BLANKET DISABLE. The obvious spelling is
`packageRules: [{matchFileNames: ['**'], enabled: false}]` plus
`vulnerabilityAlerts`, and that shape is broken upstream: Renovate 43.113.0
added a skipReason filter to flattenUpdates that drops dependencies the
vulnerability override re-enabled, so security PRs are autoclosed and none
are created (renovatebot/renovate#42655, still open on 43.120.x, closed as
not planned). includePaths restricts EXTRACTION instead, so there is no
disabled dependency to mis-filter and no rule to regress.
WHAT IS ON. The GitHub Actions pinned by SHA in our own five workflows, and
the two compose files we added. The org preset supplies the rest: the
fix(deps): prefix so a bump actually ships, digest pinning, the 7-day
cooldown with its vulnerability exemption, and the grouped-pair rules.
UPSTREAM CVEs ARE NOT RENOVATE'S JOB HERE. They surface as Dependabot
alerts and are triaged into security/overrides.yaml, which is stripped
before an upstream merge and rebuilt after, so a pin never reaches rerere.
That is the security-vs-functionality split this fork is built around; see
security/overrides.yaml for the bar an entry has to clear.
NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR LOOKING. Muting per-PR noise does not make an
inherited CVE unreal - the fork ships as a container image. The image scan
at publish and the hyperi-ci quality audit are what catch those.

packageRules.description: ClickHouse is pinned to what this fork's dev and CI stacks actually run (26.5), which is ABOVE the org preset's <26.4 LTS ceiling. The ceiling exists because dfe-infra runs 26.3.13.31 and dfe-engine writes DDL against it. Constrained to the 26.5 line rather than left open, so patches still flow and a further major cannot arrive unnoticed. Resolve the split deliberately - either this fork moves to the estate's LTS line or the estate moves up - and delete this rule when it is resolved.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: On, but not the primary net. Nothing outside includePaths is extracted, so this only ever covers our own two compose files and five workflows. Upstream's tree is covered by Dependabot alerts plus security/overrides.yaml.
